title: Extended Millimeter Emission in the HD 141569 Circumstellar Disk Detected with ALMA
question: Is there extended millimeter emission exterior to the inner disk of HD 141569, and how do the grain size distributions of the inner and outer disks compare?

evidence.quote: The 345 and 100 GHz data were published previously by (cite: white16) and (cite: white17), respectively.
a PSF subtracted HST scattered light image from (cite: konishi)

recipe.method: Annular averaging of visibilities for each frequency
key_parameters: 10 klambda bins; uncertainty is the standard deviation per bin

recipe.method: MCMC fit of a surface brightness ∝ r^-1 disk with inner and outer edges to all three data sets at once
key_parameters: Free: 345 GHz flux, spectral index, disk center, width; uniform priors flux 0.01-50 mJy, disk 0.1-300 au, index 0-4
assumptions: Flux follows a single power law in frequency

recipe.method: MCMC fit of inner and outer disks, each with own center, width and spectral index; non-overlapping
Sum flux in elliptical apertures from images, normalize and compare with HST

recipe.goal: Derive grain size distribution slope q

recipe.method: Optically thin single grain size mass, and a full size distribution mass for 10 um to 3 mm grains
assumptions: rho = 1 g/cm3, T*=10500 K, L*=24.2 Lsun, d=111 pc, albedo~0, grain radius = wavelength

evidence.quote: The inner disk ranges from approximately 16 to 45 au
the outer disk ranges from 95 to 300 au
The best fit spectral indicies of $1.81\pm0.15$ and $2.28^{+0.43}_{-0.29}$
The best fit spectral indicies of $1.81\pm0.15$ and $2.28^{+0.43}_{-0.29}$
corresponds to a grain size distribution of $q =2.95\pm0.10$

answer_key.quantity: Average reduced chi2 single vs two-component
Mass in 10 um-3 mm solids, inner and outer disk

evidence.quote: roughly 0.041 $\rm M_{\oplus}$ of small solids in the inner disk and 0.18 $\rm M_{\oplus}$ of small solids in the outer disk
For the outer disk, the best fit 345 GHz flux is 11 mJy

not_stated_but_needed: Disk inclination and position angle values used for the models and the radial profiles
Imaging parameters for the continuum images (weighting, cell, size)
Details of the 345 and 100 GHz calibration
MCMC settings (chain length, walkers, burn-in, step size)
Which channels or SPWs were used as continuum
Visibility weighting and any flux scale corrections
score_reason: Public data and a clear model, but MCMC settings, geometry and the temperature assumption are missing, and the method is inherited from earlier papers.
rediscovery_reason: Public data and numeric results, but the recipe has gaps.
